page.layout: One printed page, one column of text. Running head at top: "Cap.8o." at left and "AVGVSTINVS" at right. Below the text, a chapter heading with a woodcut ornament above it. Then the body paragraphs, with a woodcut initial A. A footnote in the same column, with mark 1, sits above the catchword "distin" at the lower right. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: dosij Iunioris imperium obierat, ad hoc tem-pus referri nō poteft. Potius in Origenistarum tempora colloco, quando tunc quoque Theodorum & Georgium Origenis fautores fuisse idem Nicephor. lib.5. cap.21. scribit, qui ipsius dogmata acutissimè acerriméque defenderunt. Statim tamen concidisse crediderim, neque illius venenum latius propagatum multis nocuis-se. Sed ad alias hæreses transcamus.
main_text.head: CAP. LXXX. Natiuitariorum error quis fuerit.

p.i: Alia sempiterne{1} natum non intelligens Filium, putat illam natiuitatem sumpsisse a tempore initium, & tamen volens coæternum Patri Filium confiteri, apud illum fuisse, antequam de illo nasceretur, existimat, hoc est, semper eum fuisse, verumtamen eum semper per Filium non fuisse: sed ex quo de illo natus est, Filium esse cœpisse. Has hæreses, quæ absque authorum nominibus sunt, putaui in hoc opus meum[?] de Philastri opere transferendas: & alias quidem[?] ipse commemorat, sed mihi appellanda hæreses non videntur. Quascunque autem[?] sine nominibus posui, nec ipse earum nomina commemorauit.

page.notes: The woodcut ornament above the heading and the woodcut initial A are not transcribed as text. Several marks after "meum", "quidem" and "autem" are doubtful and may be printed ligatures or reference signs; they are marked [?] where they affect the words. The initial "A" is joined to "lia" as "Alia". The footnote mark 1 in the text and the leading mark in the note are read as the same reference. The catchword "distin" is the start of the next page's word. Show-through from the facing page is ignored.
